subject: How can I run a sequence of mapreduce with Rhipe version 0.69

messages.author: 0c2bffd1ce4a1edd
messages.subject: How can I run a sequence of mapreduce with Rhipe version 0.69
parts:
Hi,

I want to run a loop with a mapreduce.
In each iteration the output will be used as the input to the the next iteration.
I used to do this in Rhipe 0.66 with no problem, since the command line wait until the mapreduce finish to execute the next command. 
With the new version 0.69 the mapreduce is launched and the command line run the next command without waiting the mapreduce to finish.
How can I force the command line to wait until mapreduce is finished?

Thank you

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: How can I run a sequence of mapreduce with Rhipe version 0.69
parts:
So, kindly download Rhipe again, i made some tweaks to make your life easier (i changed it today - see date). Now read the following

## Generate 1000 uniform numbers belong to id's in the range 1...10
## When this complete, run a subsequent job

## Default is mon.sec=5 which monitors every 5 seconds, users can provide functions to premptively
## kill jobs.
## here mon.sec=Inf - it just waits (and prints to output)
first.step <- rhwatch(rhmr(map=rhmap({ rhcollect(k, runif(100)) }),reduce=0,N=1000),read=FALSE,mon.sec=Inf)

if(first.step[[1]]$state !="SUCCEEDED" || first.step[[1]]$rerrors == TRUE)
  stop("Job 1 Did not Complte")

## Note how first.step is ifolder! Since no output folder was given in above
## RHIPE creates a folder in rhoptions()$HADOOP.TMP (you should set it)
## and if read=FALSE in the above call, first.step contains infor about this output folder
## you can clean the tmp folder of all these temp files with a call to 'rhclean'

next.step <-  rhwatch(rhmr(map..., ifolder=first.step),read=FALSE)

## read the results back in
final.result <- rhread(next.step)


Hope it helps
Saptarshi





[1] https://github.com/downloads/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/Rhipe_0.69.tar.gz
